construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Fire setting standard for Metal cross-polarity — the forge that refines and grants recognition
candidates.k2_overview: Your Fire moves as the Magistrate: civic light, authority that illuminates. You carry rules the way lighthouses carry flame, visibly, warmly, for everyone’s navigation. People follow your lead because it brightens rather than binds. Office becomes you. Keep the light public and tended, and rank will keep arriving on its own.
candidates.k2_functional: You carry order like a lantern: visible standards others steer by, kept lit at personal cost.

k2_domain_readings.Career: Your career runs on visible service: roles where leading and lighting are the same act. Teaching, governance, the public face of good systems. Seek podiums attached to substance.
k2_domain_readings.Status: Your standing is luminous and watched: warmth draws the credit and the scrutiny together. Live as if lit, because you are. The honest glow survives every inspection.
k2_domain_readings.Order: Your order is inspirational: people comply because you made the rule glow with purpose. That is rare governance. Write things down too. Light needs a lamp when you leave.

angles.drive: Every promise you make becomes a rule you keep. Being relied on is the closest you get to feeling safe, so you keep your word ahead of your freedom to change it. Promise a little less freely, because you keep every one you make.
angles.cost_self: Keeping a promise costs you the right to change your mind. You would rather keep a stale promise than break it, so you stay inside plans past their use. Let yourself out of one, because you turn down better offers to keep old promises.
angles.cost_others: To you, a passing promise is one to keep. Because a promise is a rule rather than a wish, you hold everyone to every one they make. Let small promises go, since you leave your friends no freedom to have only been talking.

angles.drive: By the book is the only way you trust a thing done. Since an outside rule steadies you, you go by the book ahead of the shortcut. Stay with the book, because you are the standard the work gets checked against.
angles.cost_self: Where the book and your judgment part, you side with the book. You want it done in order more than your way, so you let the book decide what you knew. Allow the book one exception, because you give up chances that cannot wait.
angles.cost_others: Doing it by the book counts as respect paid forward. Because you want it right more than fast, you hold a friend's rushed job to the book too. Name the book out loud first, since you take the easy way from everyone beside you.

angles.drive: A fairly earned title is worth more to you than any praise. Since an earned rank says you belong, you earn the next title ahead of chasing the next thrill. Let the title come slowly, because you are already doing the job it names.
angles.cost_self: Earning the title comes first, claiming it long after. You want to look deserving more than to be paid, so you earn it twice before asking once. Claim it now, because earning it this slowly leaves money you were owed on the table.
angles.cost_others: Where titles are concerned, you make everyone earn theirs too. Since an unearned rank looks like cheating, you give a colleague the long route rather than a quiet word. Say the word sometimes, because you take from them the years that earning costs.

angles.drive: A rule you learned once stays in force after it stops helping. The rules that steady you also hold you in, until you keep the correct one ahead of the useful one. You wrote most of these rules yourself, and you can retire them.
angles.cost_self: Between a rule and a chance, you take the rule. You put being correct ahead of being free, so your career keeps the rules and never jumps. Along the way, you lose out on the jobs you never went for.
angles.cost_others: Keeping to the rules is how you look after people. Because one exception feels like a collapse starting, you give them the rule ahead of what they asked for. You keep everyone at home in line and take from them the ease of being wrong.

angles.drive: Fear of slipping runs under most of what you do well. Since your standing holds your worth, you would rather never be seen to slip than be at ease. You spend more effort guarding against a slip than any slip would ever cost you.
angles.cost_self: One slip stays with you longer than with anyone who saw it. Afraid to slip, you put looking steady ahead of feeling rested, until good days tire you like bad ones. You give up your evenings to guard against slips that mostly never come.
angles.cost_others: Hiding every slip is how you serve those who depend on you. Since a visible slip reads as failed duty, you offer them a composed face ahead of a tired one. You leave them no way to help you carry it.

angles.drive: Every duty offered gets a yes before you check its cost. Since being counted on is where your standing lives, you never say no to the next request ahead of finishing the last. You pay for your standing in the strength that keeps it.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you say yes, you spend hours promised to yourself. Because holding things together comes ahead of getting home, you trade sleep for another duty. By the end of most weeks, you are short of sleep and of the strength to say yes.
angles.cost_others: Saying yes to everyone keeps your place in their lives. Because a refusal feels like lost standing, you give everyone a slice rather than anyone your whole self. You save the thinnest slice for those who need you most.

edge.lead: Fire runs through your family, your social life and your career. It is the promise made lightly that you still keep, the name people say when a thing has to be done right, and the title that fits by the time it arrives.
